explanation: The first change is hidden by physical data independence, while the second is hidden by logical data independence as long as the redesign preserves information exposed to the application. Together, those forms of independence explain why the reports continue to run.

options.text: The database relies on surrogate keys only
The system provides both physical and logical data independence
The reports are using only aggregate functions
The relation has no foreign keys

prompt: An analytics team builds reports against a customer relation. Later, the database administrator reorganizes the physical files and also renames some internal storage structures, but the relation presented to users is unchanged. A few months later, the schema is refactored in an information-preserving way, yet the same reports still run. What best explains why both changes can be tolerated?
reviewConcept: Distinguish physical and logical data independence in a multi-step scenario.
